subject: general
question: As of 28 August 2024, how many years has the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) completed since its launch?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1) 10 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on **28 August 2014**.
 
• As of 28 August 2024, PMJDY has completed **10 years** since its launch.
 
• PMJDY is a national mission aimed at ensuring access to financial services like banking, savings and deposit accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension.
 
• It is one of the world’s largest financial inclusion initiatives, aiming to provide universal access to banking facilities.
 
• The scheme was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Independence Day address on 15 August 2014.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion:**

 
 
• Financial inclusion refers to efforts to make financial products and services accessible and affordable to all individuals and businesses, regardless of their personal net worth or company size.
 
• It aims to remove barriers that exclude people from participating in the financial sector.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of PMJDY:**
 
 
• No minimum balance required.
 
• Accidental insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh and life cover of Rs. 30,000.
 
• Overdraft facility up to Rs. 10,000 is available after six months of satisfactory operation.
 
 
 
• **Impact of PMJDY:**
 
 
• As of 2024, over 48 crore bank accounts have been opened under PMJDY, with a total balance of approximately Rs. 2 lakh crore.
 
• The scheme has significantly increased the penetration of banking services in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• Lack of financial literacy among the population.
 
• Geographical barriers in reaching remote areas.
 
• Infrastructure limitations such as lack of bank branches and ATMs.
